components.text: Assess explanatory evidence through comparative Bayesian odds between equally detailed rivals on the total evidence.
Compare the priors of the fully elaborated theistic and naturalistic hypotheses rather than treating divine simplicity alone.
Replace isolated assessment of H with prior-and-likelihood odds against an equally detailed rival on total evidence.
Contest the claimed theistic simplicity advantage with a sparse naturalistic initial reality.
Explain later particles and complexity through an inherent disposition of the initial state.
Provide a comparably economical naturalistic ultimate state rather than conceding theism's simplicity advantage.
Explain later physical complexity from a simple initial state and its evolving disposition.
Challenge whether the toy initial state's productive disposition remains simple once its specific outcomes are included.
Supply a comparative likelihood reason favoring theism over the proposed naturalistic rival.
The model's apparently simple disposition must encode highly specific powers sufficient for laws, bodies, and agents.
Reject the demand for a further explanation of the initial state and laws by treating them as necessary.
Deny a broad space of alternative law systems beyond possibilities required by actual indeterminism.
Reject the assumed space of alternative initial powers by treating the actual initial state and laws as necessary.
Deny the fine-tuning comparison over many possible law systems under an actualist modal account.
Challenge the inference from human existence to a divine purpose specifically directed toward producing humans.
Contest the selection of human-producing laws as the privileged description of the cosmic outcome.
Contest treating production of humans as the uniquely salient result needing purposive explanation.
Challenge the inference from human value to a divine intention specifically explaining a universe arranged for humans.
Question whether human production is the privileged description of what cosmic conditions produce.
Offer an economical naturalistic account of consciousness rather than treating conscious agents as specially encoded outputs.
Contest the need for a distinct theistic explanation of conscious agents by identifying mental and physical processes.
The earlier move requires showing consciousness is comparatively expected under divine reasons, not merely naming a naturalistic identity theory.
Challenge identity theory by distinguishing public access to physical properties from necessary first-person access to mental life.
Identity fails because mental properties involve privileged necessary access unlike publicly accessible physical properties.
Concede for comparison that physicalism may fail while asking whether nonphysical minds can still arise naturally.
Contest the claim that any natural production of consciousness must add enough complexity to favor theism.
Even granting nonidentity, ask whether nonphysical minds can arise through a natural process without a decisive complexity penalty.
Replace a prediction of humans in every detail with a general prediction of embodied, finitely free moral agents.
Specify consciousness as part of the general class of agents theism is claimed to predict.
Replace a prediction of humans in detail with a general prediction of embodied, conscious, finitely free moral agents.
Explain why embodiment has purposive moral significance rather than being merely a substrate from which minds emerge.
Show how comparative priors and likelihoods can establish an ordering without assigning numerical probabilities.
Require agreement that one fully specified rival has the higher simplicity-based prior before dominance follows.
Treat each partition of the evidence as requiring a comparative likelihood advantage.
Show how simplicity and likelihood comparisons can yield a qualitative Bayesian ordering without numerical probabilities.
Require an agreed comparative prior advantage rather than inferring it solely from the divine zero-limit description.
Require superior likelihood across the partitioned evidence, not merely one broad successful prediction.
Reject the restricted actualist possibility space by grounding metaphysical possibility in intelligible logical alternatives.
Preserve a broad hypothesis space within which rival universes can be compared.
The necessity claim fails if intelligibly conceivable alternative universes count as logically and metaphysically possible.
Reject the inference from reasonable conceivability or belief to metaphysical possibility.
Conceivability measures reasonable belief or ignorance and therefore cannot by itself determine what metaphysically exists.
Accept an ontological notion of necessity while distinguishing it from logical or essence-based necessity.
Apply ontological necessity to whichever ultimate unexplained cause exists, whether God or universe.
Ground necessity in the unexplained ultimate reality on which everything depends rather than in logical truth or belief.
Allow either God or the universe to be the ontologically necessary ultimate brute fact.
Identify Swinburne's ontological necessity as closely resembling Oppy's metaphysical necessity.
Note their shared distinction between the relevant ontological necessity and logical necessity.
Compare the newly defined ontological necessity with the earlier metaphysical necessity terminology.
